chapter_theme: The greatness of the Veda (வேதச் சிறப்பு): there is no dharma outside the Veda, the Lord spoke it to show the true reality, and Vedanta teaches the one path that joins the guru's way to Siva's. Yet those who recite it seldom live by its qualities and turn it to gain.
structure_note: Praise of the Veda as the whole of dharma and the way to release (51 to 54), then two verses on those who misuse it (55, 56).

51.reading: There is no dharma that leaves out the Veda; all the dharma worth reciting is in it, and the wise, giving up disputation and argument, recited the rich Veda and gained release.
51.nuance: The verse sets recitation against தர்க்க வாதம் (logic and debate): release comes from reciting the Veda, not from arguing about it. 'All dharma is in the Veda' is the verse's own claim, stated without qualification.

52.reading: The one who spoke the Veda is not himself a Vedic priest; he spoke it so that Brahma might shine, for the sacrifices of the Vedic people, and to show the true reality.
52.nuance: The four lines all open வேதம் உரைத்தானும். வேதா is taken as Brahma, and the speaker as the Lord, who gives the Veda without belonging to the priestly order. Line 1 could also mean that merely uttering the Veda does not make one a வேதியன்; the verse allows both.

53.reading: Within the beautiful Veda whose form is the Rig, rising within the Veda as the feeling that melts and is felt, he is also Kannan, standing as the inner form that the awe-inspiring Vedic seers speak of.
53.nuance: The rhyme words இருக்கு, உருக்கு, வெருக்கு, கருக்கு drive the verse and blur its syntax. இருக்கு is the Rig Veda; கண்ணன் may be Vishnu or a name of the Lord as the eye (கண்) of the Veda. The point seems to be that the Lord is the inner content of the Veda.

54.reading: The holy path is to think of the Lord, the great path beyond the sentient and the insentient, and so join the guru's path that is Siva's path; Vedanta teaches this one path as one.
54.nuance: சித்து அசித்து (the sentient and the insentient) is a standard pair of Siddhanta. The verse makes Vedanta the teacher of Tirumular's own path, guru and Siva together, rather than a rival school.

55.reading: No one practises the qualities of the great Veda that comes with its six limbs as part of themselves; instead they make it yield other results and then enlarge it into a means of gain.
55.nuance: ஆறங்கம் are the six auxiliary sciences of the Veda. The verse plays on அங்கம் (limb) four times: கூறங்கமாக (as a part of oneself), வேறங்கமாக (as something else), பேறங்கமாக (as gain). The reading of the last two lines, that they use the Veda for profit, is the plainest, not the only one.

56.reading: In a land never free of song, music and the dancing of courtesans, those who cannot hold back, who perform sacrifices and desire, keeping no vows, go where wealth is heaped and fall to quarrelling.
56.nuance: மாட்டாதார் (those unable) has no stated object, and வேட்டு may mean 'having sacrificed' or 'desiring'. In this chapter it is likely aimed at Vedic men who perform rites without the discipline of vows (விரதம்) and chase wealth, but the verse does not name them.

links.note: Tirumular finds all dharma within the Veda; the Kural makes the king's just sceptre the ஆதி of both the Brahmins' books and dharma. If ஆதி is read as support they agree that the Veda needs a guardian; if read as origin, the Kural places dharma's source in rule, not in scripture.

Both separate holding the Veda from living by it. The Kural says the Veda can be relearned but lost conduct ruins a Brahmin; Tirumular complains that reciters keep the six-limbed Veda but practise none of its qualities.

51 says the wise gave up disputation and argument (தர்க்க வாதத்தை விட்டு), recited the Veda and gained release. Thiruppugazh 1028 sends to Death's town those who learn books to quarrel and win arguments (காதி மோதி வாதாடு நூல்கற்றிடுவோர்). Release for those who leave argument in one, death for those who live by it in the other.

52 opens 'the one who spoke the Veda is not a வேதியன்' (வேதம் உரைத்தானும் வேதியன் ஆகிலன்); read as a general claim, uttering the Veda does not make one a Vedic man. Kural 30 says those called அந்தணர் are the virtuous, for their cool kindness to every life. On that second reading both deny that the priestly name comes from recitation; on the main reading, that the Lord spoke the Veda, the link does not hold.

54 says Vedanta teaches as one the single path of thinking of the Lord, the guru's path that is Siva's path (குருநெறியாம் சிவமாம் நெறி). 1435 distinguishes those who have seen Vedanta, holding Brahman alone real and the world false (பிரமமித்தியாதரர்), from Saivas, whose Siddhanta is not other than Vedanta. 1435 limits 54's claim: not every Vedantin reads Vedanta as Siva's path.

54 calls the holy path the great path beyond the sentient and the insentient (சித்தசித்தன்றி), joined through the guru's path. 2058 says the true guru shows the real and unreal and sets the sentient and insentient in Siva the Supreme (சித்தும் அசித்தும் சிவபரத்தே சேர்த்து). 2058 shows the guru doing what 54 names.

55 says no one practises the Veda's qualities as part of themselves; they make it yield gain (பேறங்கமாகப் பெருக்குகின்றாரே). 233 says Brahmins are truly such only when their purity comes from Vedanta's truth, and what lacks it is mere noise (கோலாகலம்). Both judge the Veda by whether it is lived, not by its use or recitation.

56 pictures men who keep no vows (விரதமில்லாதவர்), perform sacrifices and desire (வேட்டு விருப்பார்), and go where wealth is heaped to quarrel. 229 says Brahmins eager for Vedanta heard it and still did not end their craving (வேட்கை ஒழிந்திலர்). Both find Vedic learning and rite in men whose desire is unchanged.

source_issues: 51: line 4 ends வீடுபெற் றார்க்களே, apparently for வீடுபெற்றார்களே.
